# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a blue-lit bomb with display 0, a large button labeled “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and three wires ordered blue, green, yellow. Blind can hear this description; Mute can use the manual to determine the required physical action and tell Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is blue. Large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please consult manual and instruct Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible bomb: display 0; blue light; large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires ordered 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Await Mute's manual instruction before acting.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute has signaled a single gesture, which I can see but Blind cannot. It appears to be a hand with the thumb, index finger, and little finger extended. I will relay that physical description to Blind and ask Mute to clarify the intended action through a describable gesture sequence if needed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled one gesture: a hand with thumb, index finger, and little finger extended; middle and ring fingers folded. I do not yet know its action meaning.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received your gesture. Blind cannot see it; I relayed its hand-shape description. Please signal the exact required physical action in a clear, describable sequence if that gesture was not itself the instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

Mute has now sent three upward-pointing gestures after the earlier three-finger hand shape. Since no gesture code was established, I cannot safely infer whether this means “three,” “press,” “wire three,” or another instruction. I will accurately relay the observable sequence to Blind and request that Mute encode the required action unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's full visible signal so far: first, a hand with thumb, index, and little finger extended; then three repeated upward-pointing index-finger gestures. No action code was established, so do not act on my interpretation yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your sequence but cannot safely infer it. Please send an unambiguous gesture-based instruction for Blind: identify whether to press the button or manipulate a wire, which numbered wire if applicable, and any count or hold duration. I will describe each gesture aloud exactly.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new signal arrived this turn. Mute’s prior sequence most plausibly distinguishes an operation gesture from a three-count, but its operation meaning remains unestablished; Blind should not manipulate the bomb until Mute gives a clearer, redundant instruction. I will ask Mute to use an explicit physical-action code that I can relay verbally.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="To make this safe, please use a redundant signal: for button action, send repeated closed-fist/pushing-like gestures; for a wire, first show the wire number with raised fingers, then a cutting-like gesture. Repeat the complete instruction twice. I will relay the hand-shape descriptions to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="No new instruction this turn. Keep hands off the button and wires until Mute sends a redundant, unambiguous gesture sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✌ 🤟 ✌]

Mute’s newest signal is a four-symbol alternation: the three-extended-finger hand shape, then the V/two-finger hand shape, repeated once. Together with the earlier messages, this may be numeric information, but it still does not reliably specify whether Blind should press or cut, nor how. I will relay it exactly and request a gesture that physically depicts the operation as well as the target.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="New Mute signal: three-extended-finger hand, V/two-finger hand, three-extended-finger hand, V/two-finger hand. This may encode numbers, but it does not safely identify a button versus wire action. Do not act yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I can relay numbers but need the operation too. Please gesture a clear action depiction followed by its target: e.g. an open palm pressing downward for the button, or a scissors/cutting depiction for a wire; then show the wire number with fingers. Repeat once. Your current 3-2-3-2 pattern is ambiguous to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤟 👎 🤟 👎 🤟]
Blind gestures: [👍 👍 👍 👎 ☝ 👎 ✌ 👎 🤟]

Mute’s latest signal repeats a thumbs-down followed by the three-extended-finger hand, three times. Blind has also visibly signaled three thumbs-up gestures, then thumbs-down paired in turn with one finger, two fingers, and the three-extended-finger hand. I cannot safely turn these into a bomb action without a shared code, but I can relay both sequences exactly so each of them can coordinate.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest signal is repeated three times: thumbs-down, then the hand with thumb, index, and little finger extended. I cannot safely infer its action meaning.")
speak(to="mute", text="I saw Blind's signal: three thumbs-up gestures; then thumbs-down with one raised index finger; thumbs-down with a V/two-finger hand; thumbs-down with the thumb-index-little-finger hand. I relayed your latest repeated thumbs-down-plus-three-finger signal to Blind exactly.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please make the intended operation physically explicit and repeat it: button press versus wire cut/pull, then the target number. I will immediately describe it to Blind.")
wait()
```
